statements.t: We estimate that the annual worldwide market for peripheral vascular devices exceeds $9 billion, within which we estimate that the market for our products is approximately $1 billion.
We have used acquisitions as a primary means of further penetrating the peripheral vascular device market, and we expect to continue this strategy in the future.
There can be no assurance that we will be able to do so in the future.
We expect to begin selling direct-to-hospitals in Poland starting January 2027.
We expect these plant consolidations and manufacturing transfers will result in improved control over production quality as well as reduced costs.
We intend to continue rolling out the new system in our other international locations on a staged basis.
We expect foreign currencies will represent a significant percentage of future sales.
In such cases we will record more revenue in U.S. dollars than we would have if the exchange rate had not changed.

ended September 30, 2026, we estimate that the effects of changes in foreign exchange rates increased our reported sales by approximately $2.0 million, as compared to rates in effect for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
We estimate that the stronger U.S. dollar decreased net sales by $0.4 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.
We estimate that the weaker U.S. dollar increased net sales by $2.0 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
We monitor the mix of profitability by tax jurisdiction and adjust our annual expected rate on a quarterly basis as needed.

We assess the likelihood that our deferred tax assets will be realized through future taxable income and record a valuation allowance to reduce gross deferred tax assets to an amount that we believe is more likely than not to be realized.

As of September 30, 2026, we have provided a valuation allowance of $1.7 million for deferred tax assets primarily related to Australian net operating loss and capital loss carry forwards and Massachusetts tax credit carry forwards that are not expected to be realized.
We will continue to monitor future legislative developments and assess their impact on our tax position and financial reporting.

We expect to fund any increased costs and expenditures from our existing cash and cash equivalents and short-term marketable securities, though our future capital requirements depend on numerous factors.
